content_html:
stock-tui is a mouse-first terminal stock heatmap inspired by the visual model of StockTouch. It turns a broad US equity universe into a dense 3x3 market map, lets you open a sector's top 100 companies, and then drills into a ticker with price, volume, statistics, and related news.

This is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or a continuation of StockTouch or its creators.

The client is written in Rust with Ratatui, Crossterm, Tokio, and SQLite. It is read-only: it displays market information and does not place orders.

The iterative Codex work performed through chatcode.dev is documented in the prompt-to-commit build log.

Project status: early, pre-1.0 software. The cache format and provider behavior may change between minor releases. All market information may be delayed, incomplete, or wrong. stock-tui is not investment advice.

Screenshots

These v0.2.0 captures use the deterministic offline demo at a 140x42 terminal viewport. Company identities are real SEC-catalog entries; all displayed prices, returns, volumes, rankings, and news are simulated.

Market Overview

Nine sectors, each containing 100 equally sized ticker signals, plus selectable S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq-100 ETF proxies.

Sector View

Technology ranked by estimated market cap, with one metric per tile and starred NVDA emphasized.

Ticker Detail

The one-year NVDA view with a movable chart cursor, price and time axes, volume, statistics, related news, sector rank, and absolute and relative gain.

What It Does

  • Displays nine economic sectors in a 3x3 overview, with up to 100 companies per sector.
  • Shows S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq-100 performance through the liquid SPY, DIA, and QQQ ETF proxies in the overview footer.
  • Colors tickers by period return in every ordering except Volume: losses run bright red, neutral returns gray, and gains bright green. Volume ordering instead distinguishes sectors by stable hues in color themes and uses brightness for sector-relative cumulative share volume over the selected range. Monochrome mode uses brightness only.
  • Reorders tickers by estimated market cap with SEC public-float fallback, gain, volume, or symbol.
  • Provides responsive sector grids and a ticker detail screen with a time-spaced Braille price trace, softly filled tint, price/time axes, exact cursor labels, cached-history coverage, a fine-grained volume histogram, current-order rank, statistics, concise company context, and news.
  • Supports mouse hover, clicking, wheel input, keyboard navigation, and terminal resize events.
  • Searches cached companies by symbol or company name, including retained provider assets outside the current top-100 universe.
  • Persists starred tickers and emphasizes them in every heatmap.
  • Opens immediately from a local SQLite cache while network synchronization proceeds in the background.
  • Refreshes its compact SEC-derived issuer catalog from a public R2 object, while retaining a validated catalog inside every release for offline and outage-safe startup.
  • Runs an explicitly selected demo, via --demo or onboarding, using 900 real SEC-catalog issuer identities plus three benchmark ETF identities, with deterministic, clearly labeled simulated market values.

For every ordering except Volume, the return heat scale is symmetric around zero and capped using the visible market's 90th-percentile absolute move. Volume uses a separate log scale within each sector, bounded by its 10th and 90th percentiles, so exceptional prints do not flatten brightness. 1D uses the selected snapshot's latest-session cumulative volume when available, with a cached bar-sum fallback; longer ranges sum cached OHLCV bar volume inside the selected cutoff. Range changes therefore update Volume ordering, tile values, and brightness. Missing return or range-volume data appears neutral. When the selected price endpoint is more than 72 hours old, only the ticker label is underlined as a freshness hint while retaining a contrast-aware foreground. Provider bars that explicitly describe no trading (zero volume, zero or absent trade count, and identical OHLC prices) remain in the raw cache but do not become price endpoints, refresh freshness, extend history coverage, or create a flat chart plateau.

Why Rust

Go would also be a reasonable implementation language, but Rust is a stronger fit for this client: Ratatui provides precise cell and canvas rendering support, Crossterm supplies portable mouse and keyboard events, Tokio handles background provider work, and rusqlite can bundle SQLite into one native binary. The result has no language runtime to install and keeps redraw and cache paths explicit.

Quick Start

Requirements

  • Rust 1.95 or newer for a source build
  • A native C compiler and linker for bundled SQLite and TLS dependencies
  • A modern terminal with UTF-8 and mouse reporting
  • At least 60 columns by 20 rows; 120 by 36 or larger enables the full layout
  • True-color support for the intended palette (256-color terminals still run, but color reproduction depends on the terminal)

Start the live client:

cargo run --release

Use stock-tui --help or stock-tui -h to list all command-line options.

When no credentials are configured, stock-tui shows Alpaca's registration URL as a highlighted OSC 8 terminal link and waits: press Enter to open it, c to copy it through the terminal clipboard, d to start demo mode, or Esc to continue directly to credential entry. It accepts the key ID and secret through hidden terminal input, validates the pair, and stores it under [providers.alpaca] in the platform config.toml. A complete usable pair from the process environment or a working-directory .env skips credential entry. Alpaca credentials never select a provider or override provider = "stock-api".

Use the simulated market explicitly when testing without provider data:

cargo run --release -- --demo

The first demo run selects 100 real SEC-catalog identities per sector and generates simulated prices, rankings, multiple chart timeframes, volume, and news, then stores them in SQLite. The persistent SIMULATED badge distinguishes the demo from live Alpaca data. Demo and live mode use separate default databases, demo.sqlite3 and market.sqlite3, so adding credentials after a demo run cannot combine their observations. Later runs reuse the versioned demo database. Regenerate it with:

cargo run --release -- --demo --reset-demo

--reset-demo clears the entire selected database, including favorites and any live cache, before regenerating it. This normally affects only the default demo database; use a dedicated --db path when overriding it. No Alpaca account or network connection is used in demo mode. Current versioned demo caches are reused, and the old fabricated-identity demo is upgraded automatically.

Use Alpaca Data

Alpaca's free Paper Trading account can issue credentials for the Basic market data plan; no funded brokerage account is required. To configure it:

  1. Create or sign in to an Alpaca Trading API account.
  2. Select Paper Trading in the dashboard account switcher.
  3. Open the dashboard API Keys panel and generate a key pair. Store the secret immediately: Alpaca displays it only once, and regenerating a pair invalidates the previous credentials.
  4. Launch stock-tui and enter both values when prompted. Input is not echoed, and the pair is validated before it is stored in the platform config.toml. Alternatively, put both values in the process environment, in a private .env file in the directory from which stock-tui is launched, or under [providers.alpaca] in that platform file:
ALPACA_API_KEY=your-own-key-id
ALPACA_API_SECRET=your-own-secret
[providers.alpaca]
api_key = "your-own-key-id"
api_secret = "your-own-secret"

For a source checkout, .env.example remains a ready-to-fill override:

cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env

Never commit .env, credentials, a populated database, or diagnostic output that might contain account information. Do not paste secrets into commands that will remain in shell history. Start the client with:

cargo run --release

For a prebuilt binary, run stock-tui from the private directory containing .env, or export the variables in the launching shell. The dotenv loader searches the current directory and its parents; it does not automatically search beside an installed executable. Without either override, onboarding updates <config_dir>/config.toml; find the exact directory with stock-tui --print-config and keep a populated file private. Releases before this storage change may have created <config_dir>/credentials.env; it remains a read-only fallback until the pair is saved into TOML. The app reads asset metadata from Alpaca's paper endpoint but never submits orders. If your credentials belong to another Alpaca environment, set STOCK_TUI_TRADING_URL to its matching HTTPS base URL.

The default iex feed works with Alpaca's Basic plan. See Data Providers before selecting sip or delayed_sip; access is controlled by the user's Alpaca subscription. Alpaca's current Paper Trading guide contains the authoritative dashboard steps if its interface changes.

Alpaca is the first provider adapter and remains the default. The provider is selected explicitly with --provider alpaca, STOCK_TUI_PROVIDER=alpaca, or provider = "alpaca" in config.toml. A provider-neutral HTTP adapter is also available for compatible separately operated services:

stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url http://127.0.0.1:8787

Compatible services may be unauthenticated, or may require an optional bearer token. Provider selection, base URL, optional news, and token can be kept in <config_dir>/config.toml; stock-tui --print-config shows that directory. A working-directory config.toml is not loaded automatically:

provider = "stock-api"

[providers.stock_api]
base_url = "https://stock.chatcode.dev/api"
news = true
token = "replace-with-an-out-of-band-token"

Keep a token-bearing file private and never commit it. The higher-precedence STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN environment variable is useful for temporary overrides. There is no CLI token flag, and --print-config omits both its value and presence. For a one-session private endpoint test:

read -rsp "Stock API token: " STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN
printf '\n'
export STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN
stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url https://stock.chatcode.dev/api
unset STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN

The project-operated endpoint is for explicitly authorized development tests, not a licensed public market-data service. See the Stock API HTTP Contract before operating a service. The synchronization layer keeps separate asset, market-data, and optional-news capabilities so provider payloads and authentication do not leak into storage and UI code.

To inspect the effective non-secret settings and resolved paths:

cargo run --release -- --print-config

Credentials are redacted from this output. To prohibit all network access and use an existing live-data cache:

cargo run --release -- --offline

--offline does not manufacture missing data. Run online at least once to populate a live cache, or use --demo for a self-contained experience.

Install

Prebuilt Binaries

Download the release asset for your operating system and CPU from GitHub Releases, verify it against the attached SHA256SUMS, open or extract it, and place stock-tui (or stock-tui.exe) on PATH.

Platform Release asset
Linux x86_64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
Linux ARM64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
macOS Apple Silicon stock-tui-v<VERSION>-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
macOS Intel stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
Windows x86_64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip

Tagged macOS archives contain Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime binaries accepted by Apple's notary service. A standalone command-line executable and its tar or ZIP transport cannot carry a stapled ticket, so Gatekeeper retrieves the notarization ticket online. Maintainer details are in Release Process.

The GitHub CLI can display and download the latest available assets:

gh release view --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui
gh release download --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui

Build From Source

git clone https://github.com/chatcode-lab/stock-tui.git
cd stock-tui
cargo build --release --locked
./target/release/stock-tui --demo

Install the current checkout into Cargo's binary directory:

cargo install --path . --locked
stock-tui --demo

Controls

Every visible rail control, sector, ticker, range, sort option, detail tab, and news row can be clicked with the left mouse button. The table describes normal navigation views; an open overlay owns its relevant keys as described below.

Input Action
Mouse move Select a sector, benchmark, ticker, or news row; move the chart cursor
Left click Activate the control, sector, ticker, tab, or news item
Wheel on Overview, Sector, or Starred Move to the previous or next date range
Wheel anywhere on ticker detail Move the selected chart sample
Arrow keys or h j k l Move sector, ticker, sort, chart, or news selection
Enter Open the selected sector, ticker, news item, or overlay choice
Esc Close an overlay or go up one level
Backspace Open the previous sector or ticker, wrapping at either end; delete text in Search
Space Open the next sector or ticker, wrapping at either end; insert a space in Search
/ Search cached companies by ticker or name
s Open ticker ordering
i Cycle the cell value in Sector and Starred views: price, relative gain, absolute gain, sector-relative gain, market cap, or volume
o Reverse ticker ordering in Overview, Sector, or Starred views
v Toggle Overview, Sector, and Starred heatmaps between grid and center-out clockwise spiral
F Open starred tickers
f Star or unstar the focused ticker
[ / ] Previous / next date range
= or + Zoom in one step to the next shorter date range
- Zoom out one step to the next longer date range
1 through 9 Select 1D through 10Y directly
0 Select all available history
g, then c s h e t f i m u Open Consumer, Services, Healthcare, Energy, Technology, Financial, Industrial, Materials, or Utilities
Alt/Meta + sector letter Optional direct form of the same sector shortcut
Tab Cycle Chart, Statistics, and News in compact ticker view
r Request an immediate broad-market snapshot refresh
S Open read-only data status
? Open keyboard help
q or Ctrl-C Quit and restore the terminal when no overlay is open

On ticker detail, Left/Right (or h/l) moves the chart cursor while Up/Down (or k/j) selects the related-news row; Enter opens it. Backspace and Space open the previous or next ticker in the originating sector, starred list, or benchmark order while preserving the selected range and ordering.

When the chart is wide enough, its cursor labels the selected price beside the trace intersection and the selected date or time beside the X axis. Detail headers summarize the cached price-observation span and its start. Ranges that add no older cached interval beyond the next-shorter preset are muted in the detail rail, but remain fully clickable and keep their keyboard shortcuts; ALL always means all cached history.

Sector and Starred cells show the ticker plus one selected value. Choosing an ordering resets its direction and selects its natural default value: estimated market cap, relative gain, volume, or price for alphabetical order. i then cycles the six available values independently. o reverses ticker order in Overview, Sector, and Starred views. v applies Grid or Spiral placement to the nested Overview sector heatmaps and the expanded Sector/Starred heatmaps. In ticker-selectable views, mouse targets and arrow-key navigation follow the visible layout; Overview input remains sector-level. Overview focus is exclusive: selecting one benchmark clears sector emphasis, and selecting a sector clears benchmark emphasis.

The g sector prefix applies only to the immediately following key. While it is armed, Esc or Backspace cancels it without navigating; any other non-sector key cancels the prefix and keeps its normal action. Mouse input and opening an overlay also cancel a pending prefix.

In search, type or paste a query, use Up/Down to select a result, Enter to open it, Ctrl-U to clear the query, and Esc to close. Search is local and returns at most 20 cached-company matches. Text keys, including q, digits, and range shortcuts, belong to the query while Search is open. In Help and Data Status, q closes the overlay; Esc closes every overlay. Activating a headline asks the operating system to open its provider URL in the default browser. If no browser can be launched, the URL is copied through the terminal's OSC 52 clipboard protocol instead.

During cache preparation and provider synchronization, the secondary header or footer reports numeric completed/total progress and a percentage. S opens the detailed read-only status view, while the running application version stays visible at the lower right.

On ANSI terminals, stock-tui explicitly requests all-motion tracking with SGR mouse encoding (1003 + 1006). Its click, hover, drag, and wheel reports therefore travel as text input and do not depend on legacy X10/onBinary mouse transport. On exit, reporting is disabled before raw mode is restored; pending events are drained and unread input is flushed so delayed coordinates do not leak into the next shell prompt.

Responsive Layout

  • Below 60x20, the app shows a resize prompt instead of drawing overlapping content.
  • From 60x20, compact mode keeps the action rail and adapts the number of sector columns to available width. At the exact minimum, the secondary header row collapses so every overview sector retains all five paired rows.
  • At 120x36 and above, ticker detail becomes a split workspace with chart and description on the left and statistics and news on the right.
  • The overview always preserves the 3x3 sector model. Short terminals compress each 10x10 sector into paired half-block rows so all 100 color signals remain visible. Grid and Spiral placement is preserved in both renderings.
  • Sector panels and ticker tiles use one fixed cell size at a given viewport. Any indivisible rows or columns become balanced outer padding instead of stretching selected tiles.
  • Sector tiles vertically center their ticker and selected value. Starred tiles use a thin frame when the cell is large enough and retain a compact star marker when it is not.

Terminals differ in their handling of mouse motion, Braille/half-block glyphs, OSC 8 links, OSC 52 clipboard access, and RGB color. NO_COLOR=1 stock-tui selects the monochrome palette when color is not usable.

Data And Cache

The live client combines a versioned SEC-derived candidate catalog with provider snapshots, adjusted bars, asset names/exchanges, and ticker news. It stores normalized records in a per-user SQLite database in WAL mode. At most once every 12 hours by default, a background task checks the compact catalog at https://stock.chatcode.dev/catalog/sec-catalog.json. It checks at startup and keeps that cadence while the app remains open. The first screen does not wait for the request. A valid download is cached below the platform cache directory, applied to SQLite, and followed by provider universe reconciliation; an invalid, older, unavailable, or oversized response cannot replace the last valid cache. Offline mode uses that cache when it is at least as new as the embedded release catalog, otherwise it uses the embedded catalog.

Each live cache is stamped with the active provider dataset, endpoint/feed, and market context before any rows are rendered. Switching to an incompatible provider, endpoint, feed, symbol namespace, currency, timezone, or regular session clears unattributable provider rows and checkpoints transactionally; starred symbols remain and are rehydrated by the new provider. A market context can cover several listing exchanges that share one calendar, so the current US heatmap keeps NASDAQ, NYSE, and ARCA instruments together. Only one market context is active during a launch.

Freshly generated catalogs include SEC public float as a ranking proxy, dated, provenance-tagged share bases, official SIC industry labels, and concise CC0 Wikidata company profiles anchored by SEC CIK. When a CIK points only to an administrative legal-entity stub or has no useful profile, the builder performs a bounded entity search using the normalized SEC issuer name. It accepts only an unambiguous exact identity or a conservative corporate-name shortening with matching current ticker/exchange and business evidence, then combines the item description with structured industry and, on this fallback path, product/service facts. Legal-jurisdiction boilerplate and low-information single-fact output are rejected. Roomy ticker-detail views prefer the resulting company-specific profile and retain the exchange, symbol, and SIC label as separate factual context. When no safe Wikidata identity is available, the view uses a readable SIC/listing fallback instead of presenting classification metadata as a full business description. Profile lookups and every structured fact used in the prose are stored per CIK in a durable R2 snapshot: daily catalog publications fetch new or materially renamed issuers, while a monthly full pass refreshes the slow-changing descriptions. Unambiguous filing cover facts resolve automatically; reviewed multi-class, tracking-stock, Up-C, partnership, and SPAC structures use exact class signatures, explicit multipliers, and accession-scoped issuer-reported economic facts from data/sec_share_policies.json. The builder rejects stale or structurally changed facts and fails publication if a current sector top-100 candidate loses its share basis. On startup the client refreshes candidate snapshots and prefers a valid provider-supplied market cap. Otherwise, a provider with corporate-action coverage adjusts the catalog share basis for forward and reverse splits after its as-of date before multiplying by the current price. If the required split lookup fails, the local estimate remains unavailable instead of combining stale shares with a post-split price. Each sector's top 100 is then selected by estimated cap or numeric public float when cap is unavailable. Public float is never displayed as market cap. It then resumes two years of daily bars plus all provider-available weekly history for the selected 900 companies and the three benchmark ETF proxies. Both history plans use a seven-day overlap after their initial backfill. It lazily requests range-appropriate bars and 20 newest headlines when a ticker is opened. Beyond the special 1D snapshot case, heatmap volume prefers daily bars through 2Y and weekly bars for 5Y, 10Y, and ALL, with cached alternative timeframes used only when the preferred aggregate is unavailable. Ticker-detail statistics continue to show latest-session snapshot volume, while solid chart bars use traded provider volume without manufacturing data for price-only endpoints. After the first positive volume bar, unoccupied columns repeat the preceding height in a dim visual trail through the last rendered price column; the future part of an ongoing session remains blank. This does not change cached volume, statistics, aggregation, or scale. 1D draws the latest observed regular session across its full exchange-local trading window, leaving the future price trace blank. 1W concatenates the five latest observed sessions, and the other intraday view omits closed periods; daily and weekly histories use ordinal observations. Long gaps during an open session carry the last traded price to the next observation. Session membership is calculated in the configured market timezone and labels are shown in the user's local timezone. In live mode, the broad-market snapshot refresh runs immediately on startup and every five minutes by default; r starts one immediately and restarts that timer. Opening a ticker or changing its range separately triggers a lazy detail request. Demo and offline modes never schedule remote refreshes. S only opens the status panel; it does not start synchronization.

The default Alpaca adapter is limited to US equities. Its feed selection changes US venue coverage; it does not enable non-US markets. The stock-api contract is provider-neutral, but the current sector catalog and UI remain designed around US-listed equities and USD. Additional countries, currencies, sessions, and licensed sources require compatible adapters and explicit product support. The public catalog endpoint contains only the compact SEC-derived issuer catalog; it is not a market-price or news proxy.

Alpaca's Basic plan currently provides a 200 historical-request-per-minute limit and real-time US equity coverage from IEX, a single exchange. The default client limiter is 180 requests per minute. IEX prices and volumes are not the same as consolidated whole-market SIP figures. Provider limits and terms can change; consult Alpaca's current documentation.

The local cache is for the credential holder's use. Alpaca states that its API data cannot be redistributed under ordinary access terms. Do not publish or ship a populated Alpaca cache. The default production model is bring-your-own-key and there is no public shared-key price/news service. The separately operated stock-api endpoint is restricted to explicitly authorized development tests and is not a licensed public market-data backend. See Requesting Public-Display Permission before proposing any no-key service.

See Cache and Sync for the schema and lifecycle, and Configuration for every supported option.

Sector Model

The project intentionally preserves StockTouch's nine-sector presentation: Consumer, Services, Healthcare, Energy, Technology, Financial, Industrial, Materials, and Utilities. This is a legacy visualization taxonomy, not the current 11-sector GICS taxonomy. For example, Communication Services maps to Services and Real Estate maps to Financial. Mapping and catalog caveats are documented in Data Providers.

Development

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-targets --all-features

Provider tests use controlled local fixtures and must never use real secrets. See CONTRIBUTING.md before proposing a new data source or changing the sector taxonomy.

Financial Disclaimer

stock-tui is an informational visualization project, not a broker, exchange, investment adviser, research provider, or source of official quotations. It does not account for every venue, corporate action, symbol change, data error, or latency condition. Demo values are simulated. Historical performance does not predict future results. Verify important information with an authorized source and make financial decisions independently.

Alternatively, put both values in the process environment, in a private .env file in the directory from which stock-tui is launched, or under [providers.alpaca] in that platform file: ALPACA_API_KEY=your-own-key-id ALPACA_API_SECRET=your-own-secret [providers.alpaca] api_key = "your-own-key-id" api_secret = "your-own-secret" For a source checkout, .env.example remains a ready-to-fill override: cp .env.example .env chmod 600 .env Never commit .env, credentials, a populated database, or diagnostic output that might contain account information. Do not paste secrets into commands that will remain in shell history. Start the client with: cargo run --release For a prebuilt binary, run stock-tui from the private directory containing .env, or export the variables in the launching shell. The dotenv loader searches the current directory and its parents; it does not automatically search beside an installed executable. Without either override, onboarding updates <config_dir>/config.toml; find the exact directory with stock-tui --print-config and keep a populated file private. Releases before this storage change may have created <config_dir>/credentials.env; it remains a read-only fallback until the pair is saved into TOML. The app reads asset metadata from Alpaca's paper endpoint but never submits orders. If your credentials belong to another Alpaca environment, set STOCK_TUI_TRADING_URL to its matching HTTPS base URL. The default iex feed works with Alpaca's Basic plan. See Data Providers before selecting sip or delayed_sip; access is controlled by the user's Alpaca subscription. Alpaca's current Paper Trading guide contains the authoritative dashboard steps if its interface changes. Alpaca is the first provider adapter and remains the default. The provider is selected explicitly with --provider alpaca, STOCK_TUI_PROVIDER=alpaca, or provider = "alpaca" in config.toml. A provider-neutral HTTP adapter is also available for compatible separately operated services: stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url http://127.0.0.1:8787 Compatible services may be unauthenticated, or may require an optional bearer token. Provider selection, base URL, optional news, and token can be kept in <config_dir>/config.toml; stock-tui --print-config shows that directory. A working-directory config.toml is not loaded automatically: provider = "stock-api" [providers.stock_api] base_url = "https://stock.chatcode.dev/api" news = true token = "replace-with-an-out-of-band-token" Keep a token-bearing file private and never commit it. The higher-precedence STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN environment variable is useful for temporary overrides. There is no CLI token flag, and --print-config omits both its value and presence. For a one-session private endpoint test: read -rsp "Stock API token: " STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN printf '\n' export STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url https://stock.chatcode.dev/api unset STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN The project-operated endpoint is for explicitly authorized development tests, not a licensed public market-data service. See the Stock API HTTP Contract before operating a service. The synchronization layer keeps separate asset, market-data, and optional-news capabilities so provider payloads and authentication do not leak into storage and UI code. To inspect the effective non-secret settings and resolved paths: cargo run --release -- --print-config Credentials are redacted from this output. To prohibit all network access and use an existing live-data cache: cargo run --release -- --offline --offline does not manufacture missing data. Run online at least once to populate a live cache, or use --demo for a self-contained experience. Install Prebuilt Binaries Download the release asset for your operating system and CPU from GitHub Releases, verify it against the attached SHA256SUMS, open or extract it, and place stock-tui (or stock-tui.exe) on PATH. Platform Release asset Linux x86_64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz Linux ARM64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz macOS Apple Silicon stock-tui-v<VERSION>-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz macOS Intel stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz Windows x86_64 stock-tui-v<VERSION>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip Tagged macOS archives contain Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime binaries accepted by Apple's notary service. A standalone command-line executable and its tar or ZIP transport cannot carry a stapled ticket, so Gatekeeper retrieves the notarization ticket online. Maintainer details are in Release Process. The GitHub CLI can display and download the latest available assets: gh release view --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui gh release download --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui Build From Source git clone https://github.com/chatcode-lab/stock-tui.git cd stock-tui cargo build --release --locked ./target/release/stock-tui --demo Install the current checkout into Cargo's binary directory: cargo install --path . --locked stock-tui --demo Controls Every visible rail control, sector, ticker, range, sort option, detail tab, and news row can be clicked with the left mouse button. The table describes normal navigation views; an open overlay owns its relevant keys as described below. Input Action Mouse move Select a sector, benchmark, ticker, or news row; move the chart cursor Left click Activate the control, sector, ticker, tab, or news item Wheel on Overview, Sector, or Starred Move to the previous or next date range Wheel anywhere on ticker detail Move the selected chart sample Arrow keys or h j k l Move sector, ticker, sort, chart, or news selection Enter Open the selected sector, ticker, news item, or overlay choice Esc Close an overlay or go up one level Backspace Open the previous sector or ticker, wrapping at either end; delete text in Search Space Open the next sector or ticker, wrapping at either end; insert a space in Search / Search cached companies by ticker or name s Open ticker ordering i Cycle the cell value in Sector and Starred views: price, relative gain, absolute gain, sector-relative gain, market cap, or volume o Reverse ticker ordering in Overview, Sector, or Starred views v Toggle Overview, Sector, and Starred heatmaps between grid and center-out clockwise spiral F Open starred tickers f Star or unstar the focused ticker [ / ] Previous / next date range = or + Zoom in one step to the next shorter date range - Zoom out one step to the next longer date range 1 through 9 Select 1D through 10Y directly 0 Select all available history g, then c s h e t f i m u Open Consumer, Services, Healthcare, Energy, Technology, Financial, Industrial, Materials, or Utilities Alt/Meta + sector letter Optional direct form of the same sector shortcut Tab Cycle Chart, Statistics, and News in compact ticker view r Request an immediate broad-market snapshot refresh S Open read-only data status ? Open keyboard help q or Ctrl-C Quit and restore the terminal when no overlay is open On ticker detail, Left/Right (or h/l) moves the chart cursor while Up/Down (or k/j) selects the related-news row; Enter opens it. Backspace and Space open the previous or next ticker in the originating sector, starred list, or benchmark order while preserving the selected range and ordering. When the chart is wide enough, its cursor labels the selected price beside the trace intersection and the selected date or time beside the X axis. Detail headers summarize the cached price-observation span and its start. Ranges that add no older cached interval beyond the next-shorter preset are muted in the detail rail, but remain fully clickable and keep their keyboard shortcuts; ALL always means all cached history. Sector and Starred cells show the ticker plus one selected value. Choosing an ordering resets its direction and selects its natural default value: estimated market cap, relative gain, volume, or price for alphabetical order. i then cycles the six available values independently. o reverses ticker order in Overview, Sector, and Starred views. v applies Grid or Spiral placement to the nested Overview sector heatmaps and the expanded Sector/Starred heatmaps. In ticker-selectable views, mouse targets and arrow-key navigation follow the visible layout; Overview input remains sector-level. Overview focus is exclusive: selecting one benchmark clears sector emphasis, and selecting a sector clears benchmark emphasis. The g sector prefix applies only to the immediately following key. While it is armed, Esc or Backspace cancels it without navigating; any other non-sector key cancels the prefix and keeps its normal action. Mouse input and opening an overlay also cancel a pending prefix. In search, type or paste a query, use Up/Down to select a result, Enter to open it, Ctrl-U to clear the query, and Esc to close. Search is local and returns at most 20 cached-company matches. Text keys, including q, digits, and range shortcuts, belong to the query while Search is open. In Help and Data Status, q closes the overlay; Esc closes every overlay. Activating a headline asks the operating system to open its provider URL in the default browser. If no browser can be launched, the URL is copied through the terminal's OSC 52 clipboard protocol instead. During cache preparation and provider synchronization, the secondary header or footer reports numeric completed/total progress and a percentage. S opens the detailed read-only status view, while the running application version stays visible at the lower right. On ANSI terminals, stock-tui explicitly requests all-motion tracking with SGR mouse encoding (1003 + 1006). Its click, hover, drag, and wheel reports therefore travel as text input and do not depend on legacy X10/onBinary mouse transport. On exit, reporting is disabled before raw mode is restored; pending events are drained and unread input is flushed so delayed coordinates do not leak into the next shell prompt. Responsive Layout Below 60x20, the app shows a resize prompt instead of drawing overlapping content. From 60x20, compact mode keeps the action rail and adapts the number of sector columns to available width. At the exact minimum, the secondary header row collapses so every overview sector retains all five paired rows. At 120x36 and above, ticker detail becomes a split workspace with chart and description on the left and statistics and news on the right. The overview always preserves the 3x3 sector model. Short terminals compress each 10x10 sector into paired half-block rows so all 100 color signals remain visible. Grid and Spiral placement is preserved in both renderings. Sector panels and ticker tiles use one fixed cell size at a given viewport. Any indivisible rows or columns become balanced outer padding instead of stretching selected tiles. Sector tiles vertically center their ticker and selected value. Starred tiles use a thin frame when the cell is large enough and retain a compact star marker when it is not. Terminals differ in their handling of mouse motion, Braille/half-block glyphs, OSC 8 links, OSC 52 clipboard access, and RGB color. NO_COLOR=1 stock-tui selects the monochrome palette when color is not usable. Data And Cache The live client combines a versioned SEC-derived candidate catalog with provider snapshots, adjusted bars, asset names/exchanges, and ticker news. It stores normalized records in a per-user SQLite database in WAL mode. At most once every 12 hours by default, a background task checks the compact catalog at https://stock.chatcode.dev/catalog/sec-catalog.json. It checks at startup and keeps that cadence while the app remains open. The first screen does not wait for the request. A valid download is cached below the platform cache directory, applied to SQLite, and followed by provider universe reconciliation; an invalid, older, unavailable, or oversized response cannot replace the last valid cache. Offline mode uses that cache when it is at least as new as the embedded release catalog, otherwise it uses the embedded catalog. Each live cache is stamped with the active provider dataset, endpoint/feed, and market context before any rows are rendered. Switching to an incompatible provider, endpoint, feed, symbol namespace, currency, timezone, or regular session clears unattributable provider rows and checkpoints transactionally; starred symbols remain and are rehydrated by the new provider. A market context can cover several listing exchanges that share one calendar, so the current US heatmap keeps NASDAQ, NYSE, and ARCA instruments together. Only one market context is active during a launch. Freshly generated catalogs include SEC public float as a ranking proxy, dated, provenance-tagged share bases, official SIC industry labels, and concise CC0 Wikidata company profiles anchored by SEC CIK. When a CIK points only to an administrative legal-entity stub or has no useful profile, the builder performs a bounded entity search using the normalized SEC issuer name. It accepts only an unambiguous exact identity or a conservative corporate-name shortening with matching current ticker/exchange and business evidence, then combines the item description with structured industry and, on this fallback path, product/service facts. Legal-jurisdiction boilerplate and low-information single-fact output are rejected. Roomy ticker-detail views prefer the resulting company-specific profile and retain the exchange, symbol, and SIC label as separate factual context. When no safe Wikidata identity is available, the view uses a readable SIC/listing fallback instead of presenting classification metadata as a full business description. Profile lookups and every structured fact used in the prose are stored per CIK in a durable R2 snapshot: daily catalog publications fetch new or materially renamed issuers, while a monthly full pass refreshes the slow-changing descriptions. Unambiguous filing cover facts resolve automatically; reviewed multi-class, tracking-stock, Up-C, partnership, and SPAC structures use exact class signatures, explicit multipliers, and accession-scoped issuer-reported economic facts from data/sec_share_policies.json. The builder rejects stale or structurally changed facts and fails publication if a current sector top-100 candidate loses its share basis. On startup the client refreshes candidate snapshots and prefers a valid provider-supplied market cap. Otherwise, a provider with corporate-action coverage adjusts the catalog share basis for forward and reverse splits after its as-of date before multiplying by the current price. If the required split lookup fails, the local estimate remains unavailable instead of combining stale shares with a post-split price. Each sector's top 100 is then selected by estimated cap or numeric public float when cap is unavailable. Public float is never displayed as market cap. It then resumes two years of daily bars plus all provider-available weekly history for the selected 900 companies and the three benchmark ETF proxies. Both history plans use a seven-day overlap after their initial backfill. It lazily requests range-appropriate bars and 20 newest headlines when a ticker is opened. Beyond the special 1D snapshot case, heatmap volume prefers daily bars through 2Y and weekly bars for 5Y, 10Y, and ALL, with cached alternative timeframes used only when the preferred aggregate is unavailable. Ticker-detail statistics continue to show latest-session snapshot volume, while solid chart bars use traded provider volume without manufacturing data for price-only endpoints. After the first positive volume bar, unoccupied columns repeat the preceding height in a dim visual trail through the last rendered price column; the future part of an ongoing session remains blank. This does not change cached volume, statistics, aggregation, or scale. 1D draws the latest observed regular session across its full exchange-local trading window, leaving the future price trace blank. 1W concatenates the five latest observed sessions, and the other intraday view omits closed periods; daily and weekly histories use ordinal observations. Long gaps during an open session carry the last traded price to the next observation. Session membership is calculated in the configured market timezone and labels are shown in the user's local timezone. In live mode, the broad-market snapshot refresh runs immediately on startup and every five minutes by default; r starts one immediately and restarts that timer. Opening a ticker or changing its range separately triggers a lazy detail request. Demo and offline modes never schedule remote refreshes. S only opens the status panel; it does not start synchronization. The default Alpaca adapter is limited to US equities. Its feed selection changes US venue coverage; it does not enable non-US markets. The stock-api contract is provider-neutral, but the current sector catalog and UI remain designed around US-listed equities and USD. Additional countries, currencies, sessions, and licensed sources require compatible adapters and explicit product support. The public catalog endpoint contains only the compact SEC-derived issuer catalog; it is not a market-price or news proxy. Alpaca's Basic plan currently provides a 200 historical-request-per-minute limit and real-time US equity coverage from IEX, a single exchange. The default client limiter is 180 requests per minute. IEX prices and volumes are not the same as consolidated whole-market SIP figures. Provider limits and terms can change; consult Alpaca's current documentation. The local cache is for the credential holder's use. Alpaca states that its API data cannot be redistributed under ordinary access terms. Do not publish or ship a populated Alpaca cache. The default production model is bring-your-own-key and there is no public shared-key price/news service. The separately operated stock-api endpoint is restricted to explicitly authorized development tests and is not a licensed public market-data backend. See Requesting Public-Display Permission before proposing any no-key service. See Cache and Sync for the schema and lifecycle, and Configuration for every supported option. Sector Model The project intentionally preserves StockTouch's nine-sector presentation: Consumer, Services, Healthcare, Energy, Technology, Financial, Industrial, Materials, and Utilities. This is a legacy visualization taxonomy, not the current 11-sector GICS taxonomy. For example, Communication Services maps to Services and Real Estate maps to Financial. Mapping and catalog caveats are documented in Data Providers. blocks.html_en: The live client combines a versioned SEC-derived candidate catalog with provider snapshots, adjusted bars, asset names/exchanges, and ticker news. It stores normalized records in a per-user SQLite database in WAL mode. At most once every 12 hours by default, a background task checks the compact catalog at https://stock.chatcode.dev/catalog/sec-catalog.json. It checks at startup and keeps that cadence while the app remains open. The first screen does not wait for the request. A valid download is cached below the platform cache directory, applied to SQLite, and followed by provider universe reconciliation; an invalid, older, unavailable, or oversized response cannot replace the last valid cache. blocks.html_en: Freshly generated catalogs include SEC public float as a ranking proxy, dated, provenance-tagged share bases, official SIC industry labels, and concise CC0 Wikidata company profiles anchored by SEC CIK. When a CIK points only to an administrative legal-entity stub or has no useful profile, the builder performs a bounded entity search using the normalized SEC issuer name. It accepts only an unambiguous exact identity or a conservative corporate-name shortening with matching current ticker/exchange and business evidence, then combines the item description with structured industry and, on this fallback path, product/service facts. Legal-jurisdiction boilerplate and low-information single-fact output are rejected. Roomy ticker-detail views prefer the resulting company-specific profile and retain the exchange, symbol, and SIC label as separate factual context. When no safe Wikidata identity is available, the view uses a readable SIC/listing fallback instead of presenting classification metadata as a full business description. Profile lookups and every structured fact used in the prose are stored per CIK in a durable R2 snapshot: daily catalog publications fetch new or materially renamed issuers, while a monthly full pass refreshes the slow-changing descriptions. Unambiguous filing cover facts resolve automatically; reviewed multi-class, tracking-stock, Up-C, partnership, and SPAC structures use exact class signatures, explicit multipliers, and accession-scoped issuer-reported economic facts from data/sec_share_policies.json. The builder rejects stale or structurally changed facts and fails publication if a current sector top-100 candidate loses its share basis. On startup the client refreshes candidate snapshots and prefers a valid provider-supplied market cap. Otherwise, a provider with corporate-action coverage adjusts the catalog share basis for forward and reverse splits after its as-of date before multiplying by the current price. If the required split lookup fails, the local estimate remains unavailable instead of combining stale shares with a post-split price. Each sector's top 100 is then selected by estimated cap or numeric public float when cap is unavailable. Public float is never displayed as market cap. It then resumes two years of daily bars plus all provider-available weekly history for the selected 900 companies and the three benchmark ETF proxies. Both history plans use a seven-day overlap after their initial backfill. It lazily requests range-appropriate bars and 20 newest headlines when a ticker is opened. Beyond the special 1D snapshot case, heatmap volume prefers daily bars through 2Y and weekly bars for 5Y, 10Y, and ALL, with cached alternative timeframes used only when the preferred aggregate is unavailable. Ticker-detail statistics continue to show latest-session snapshot volume, while solid chart bars use traded provider volume without manufacturing data for price-only endpoints. After the first positive volume bar, unoccupied columns repeat the preceding height in a dim visual trail through the last rendered price column; the future part of an ongoing session remains blank. This does not change cached volume, statistics, aggregation, or scale. 1D draws the latest observed regular session across its full exchange-local trading window, leaving the future price trace blank. 1W concatenates the five latest observed sessions, and the other intraday view omits closed periods; daily and weekly histories use ordinal observations. Long gaps during an open session carry the last traded price to the next observation. Session membership is calculated in the configured market timezone and labels are shown in the user's local timezone. In live mode, the broad-market snapshot refresh runs immediately on startup and every five minutes by default; r starts one immediately and restarts that timer. Opening a ticker or changing its range separately triggers a lazy detail request. Demo and offline modes never schedule remote refreshes. S only opens the status panel; it does not start synchronization.

content_html_zh:
stock-tui 是一个鼠标优先的终端股票热图，灵感来自 StockTouch 的视觉模型。 它将广阔的美国股票世界转变为密集的 3x3 市场地图，让您打开某个行业的前 100 家公司，然后深入了解价格、成交​​量、统计数据和相关新闻的股票行情。

这是一个独立的开源项目。 它不隶属于 StockTouch 或其创建者，也不受其认可或延续。

客户端是用 Rust 编写的，包括 Ratatui、Crossterm、Tokio 和 SQLite。 它是只读的：它显示市场信息并且不下订单。

通过 chatcode.dev 执行的迭代 Codex 工作记录在提示提交构建日志中。

项目状态：早期，1.0 版本之前的软件。 缓存格式和提供程序行为可能会在次要版本之间发生变化。 所有市场信息可能有延迟、不完整或错误。 stock-tui 不是投资建议。

截图

这些 v0.2.0 捕获在 140x42 终端视口中使用确定性离线演示。 公司身份是真实的 SEC 目录条目；所有显示的价格、回报、交易量、排名和新闻都是模拟的。

市场概况

九个板块，每个板块包含 100 个同等大小的股票信号，以及可选的 S&P 500、Dow 和 Nasdaq-100 ETF 代理。

扇形视图

按估计市值对技术进行排名，每个板块有一个指标，并强调带星号的 NVDA。

股票详细信息

一年期 NVDA 视图，带有可移动图表光标、价格和时间轴、交易量、统计数据、相关新闻、行业排名以及绝对和相对收益。

它的作用

  • 以 3x3 概览显示 9 个经济部门，每个部门最多 100 家公司。
  • 通过概览页脚中的流动 SPY、DIA 和 QQQ ETF 代理显示标准普尔 500、道琼斯指数和纳斯达克 100 指数的表现。
  • 除交易量外，每个订单中的周期回报均以颜色显示：损失为亮红色，中性回报为灰色，收益为亮绿色。 相反，成交量排序通过颜色主题中的稳定色调来区分扇区，并使用选定范围内扇区相对累计份额的亮度。 单色模式仅使用亮度。
  • 根据 SEC 公众流通量回落、增益、交易量或代码，按估计市值重新排序股票。
  • 提供响应式行业网格和股票详细信息屏幕，其中包含时间间隔盲文价格轨迹、柔和填充的色调、价格/时间轴、精确的光标标签、缓存的历史覆盖范围、细粒度的交易量直方图、当前订单排名、统计数据、简洁的公司背景和新闻。
  • 支持鼠标悬停、单击、滚轮输入、键盘导航和终端调整大小事件。
  • 按代码或公司名称搜索缓存的公司，包括当前前 100 名范围之外的保留提供商资产。
  • 保留加星标的股票并在每个热图中强调它们。
  • 立即从本地 SQLite 缓存打开，同时网络同步在后台进行。
  • 从公共 R2 对象刷新其紧凑的 SEC 派生发行人目录，同时在每个版本中保留经过验证的目录，以实现离线和断电安全启动。
  • 通过 --demo 或 onboarding 运行明确选择的演示，使用 900 个真实的 SEC 目录发行人身份以及三个基准 ETF 身份，并具有确定性、明确标记的模拟市场价值。

对于除交易量之外的每个排序，返回热度在零附近对称，并使用可见市场的 90% 绝对移动来限制。 体积在每个扇区中使用单独的对数刻度，以第 10 个和第 90 个百分位数为界，因此出色的打印不会使亮度变平。 1D 使用所选快照的最新会话累积量（如果可用），并带有缓存的条形总和后备；较长范围内所选截止值内缓存的 OHLCV 条形体积总和。 因此，范围更改会更新体积排序、平铺值和亮​​度。 缺少回报或范围体积数据似乎是中性的。 当所选价格端点已存在超过 72 小时时，只有股票代码标签带有下划线作为新鲜度提示，同时保留对比感知前景。 明确描述无交易（零交易量、零或不存在交易计数以及相同的 OHLC 价格）的提供商条形图仍保留在原始缓存中，但不会成为价格端点、刷新新鲜度、扩展历史覆盖范围或创建平面图表平台。

为什么生锈

Go 也是一种合理的实现语言，但 Rust 更适合这个客户端：Ratatui 提供精确的单元格和画布渲染支持，Crossterm 提供便携式鼠标和键盘事件，Tokio 处理后台提供程序工作，而 rusqlite 可以将 SQLite 捆绑到一个本机二进制文件中。 结果无需安装语言运行时，并保持重绘和缓存路径明确。

快速入门

要求

  • Rust 1.95 或更高版本用于源构建
  • 用于捆绑 SQLite 和 TLS 依赖项的本机 C 编译器和链接器
  • 具有 UTF-8 和鼠标报告功能的现代终端
  • 至少 60 列 x 20 行； 120 x 36 或更大可实现完整布局
  • 对预期调色板的真彩色支持（256 色终端仍然运行，但颜色再现取决于终端）

启动实时客户端：

cargo run --release

使用 stock-tui --help 或 stock-tui -h 列出所有命令行选项。

当未配置凭据时，stock-tui 将 Alpaca 的注册 URL 显示为突出显示的 OSC 8 终端链接并等待：按 Enter 键打开它，按 c 通过终端剪贴板复制它，按 d 启动演示模式，或按 Esc 直接继续输入凭据。 它通过隐藏的终端输入接受密钥 ID 和密钥，验证该对，并将其存储在平台 config.toml 的 [providers.alpaca] 下。 进程环境或工作目录 .env 中的完整可用对会跳过凭据条目。 Alpaca 凭证永远不会选择提供商或覆盖提供商 =“stock-api”。

在没有提供商数据的情况下进行测试时明确使用模拟市场：

cargo run --release -- --demo

第一个演示运行为每个部门选择 100 个真实的 SEC 目录身份，并生成模拟价格、排名、多个图表时间范围、交易量和新闻，然后将它们存储在 SQLite 中。 持久的 SIMULATED 徽章将演示与实时羊驼数据区分开来。 演示和实时模式使用单独的默认数据库 demo.sqlite3 和 market.sqlite3，因此在演示运行后添加凭据无法合并它们的观察结果。 稍后的运行将重用版本化演示数据库。 重新生成它：

cargo run --release -- --demo --reset-demo

--reset-demo 在重新生成之前清除整个选定的数据库，包括收藏夹和任何实时缓存。 这通常只影响默认的演示数据库；覆盖它时使用专用的 --db 路径。 演示模式下不使用 Alpaca 帐户或网络连接。 当前版本的演示缓存将被重用，旧的身份演示将自动升级。

使用羊驼数据

Alpaca的免费模拟交易账户可以签发基本市场数据计划的凭证；不需要有资金的经纪账户。 配置它：

  1. 创建或登录 Alpaca Trading API 帐户。
  2. 在仪表板账户切换器中选择模拟交易。
  3. 打开仪表板 API 密钥面板并生成密钥对。 立即存储秘密：Alpaca 仅显示一次，重新生成一对会使之前的凭据失效。
  4. 启动 stock-tui 并在出现提示时输入这两个值。 输入不会被回显，并且在将其存储在平台 config.toml 中之前会验证该对。 或者，将这两个值放入进程环境中、启动 stock-tui 的目录中的私有 .env 文件中或该平台文件中的 [providers.alpaca] 下：
ALPACA_API_KEY=your-own-key-id
ALPACA_API_SECRET=your-own-secret
[providers.alpaca]
api_key = "your-own-key-id"
api_secret = "your-own-secret"

对于源签出，.env.example 仍然是一个准备填充的覆盖：

cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env

切勿提交可能包含帐户信息的 .env、凭据、填充的数据库或诊断输出。 不要将机密粘贴到将保留在 shell 历史记录中的命令中。 启动客户端：

cargo run --release

对于预构建的二进制文件，请从包含 .env 的私有目录运行 stock-tui，或导出启动 shell 中的变量。 dotenv 加载器搜索当前目录及其父目录；它不会自动搜索已安装的可执行文件旁边。 如果没有任何覆盖，载入更新 <config_dir>/config.toml；使用 stock-tui --print-config 找到确切的目录并将填充的文件保密。 此存储更改之前的版本可能已创建 <config_dir>/credentials.env；它仍然是只读后备，直到该对保存到 TOML 中。 该应用程序从 Alpaca 的纸质端点读取资产元数据，但从不提交订单。 如果您的凭据属于另一个 Alpaca 环境，请将 STOCK_TUI_TRADING_URL 设置为其匹配的 HTTPS 基本 URL。

默认的 iex feed 适用于 Alpaca 的基本计划。 选择sip或delayed_sip之前请参阅数据提供商；访问权限由用户的 Alpaca 订阅控制。 如果界面发生变化，Alpaca 当前的模拟交易指南包含权威的仪表板步骤。

Alpaca 是第一个提供者适配器并且仍然是默认适配器。 使用 --provider alpaca、STOCK_TUI_PROVIDER=alpaca 或 config.toml 中的provider =“alpaca”显式选择提供程序。 提供商中立的 HTTP 适配器也可用于兼容的单独运营的服务：

stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url http://127.0.0.1:8787

兼容的服务可能未经身份验证，或者可能需要可选的承载令牌。 提供者选择、基本 URL、可选新闻和令牌可以保存在 <config_dir>/config.toml 中； stock-tui --print-config 显示该目录。 工作目录 config.toml 不会自动加载：

provider = "stock-api"

[providers.stock_api]
base_url = "https://stock.chatcode.dev/api"
news = true
token = "replace-with-an-out-of-band-token"

将带有令牌的文件保持私有并且永远不要提交它。 较高优先级的 STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN 环境变量对于临时覆盖很有用。 没有 CLI 令牌标志，并且 --print-config 忽略了它的值和存在。 对于单会话专用端点测试：

read -rsp "Stock API token: " STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN
printf '\n'
export STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN
stock-tui --provider stock-api --stock-api-url https://stock.chatcode.dev/api
unset STOCK_TUI_STOCK_API_TOKEN

项目运营的端点用于明确授权的开发测试，而不是许可的公共市场数据服务。 在操作服务之前请参阅 Stock API HTTP 合同。 同步层保留单独的资产、市场数据和可选新闻功能，因此提供者有效负载和身份验证不会泄漏到存储和 UI 代码中。

要检查有效的非秘密设置和解析路径：

cargo run --release -- --print-config

凭据是从此输出中编辑的。 要禁止所有网络访问并使用现有的实时数据缓存：

cargo run --release -- --offline

--offline 不制造缺失数据。 至少在线运行一次以填充实时缓存，或使用 --demo 获得独立的体验。

安装

预构建的二进制文件

从 GitHub Releases 下载适用于您的操作系统和 CPU 的发布资产，根据附加的 SHA256SUMS 进行验证，打开或解压它，并将 stock-tui （或 stock-tui.exe）放在 PATH 上。

平台 释放资产
Linux x86_64 stock-tui-v<版本>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
LinuxARM64 stock-tui-v<版本>-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
macOS 苹果芯片 stock-tui-v<版本>-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
macOS 英特尔 stock-tui-v<版本>-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
Windows x86_64 stock-tui-v<版本>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip

标记的 macOS 存档包含 Apple 公证服务接受的开发人员 ID 签名、强化运行时二进制文件。 独立的命令行可执行文件及其 tar 或 ZIP 传输无法携带装订票据，因此 Gatekeeper 在线检索公证票据。 维护者详细信息位于发布流程中。

GitHub CLI 可以显示和下载最新的可用资产：

gh release view --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui
gh release download --repo chatcode-lab/stock-tui

从源代码构建

git clone https://github.com/chatcode-lab/stock-tui.git
cd stock-tui
cargo build --release --locked
./target/release/stock-tui --demo

将当前的 checkout 安装到 Cargo 的二进制目录中：

cargo install --path . --locked
stock-tui --demo

控制

每个可见的轨道控件、扇区、股票行情、范围、排序选项、详细信息选项卡和新闻行都可以用鼠标左键单击。 该表描述了正常的导航视图；开放的覆盖层拥有其相关的键，如下所述。

Input 行动
鼠标移动 选择行业、基准、股票行情或新闻行；移动图表光标
左键单击 激活控件、扇区、股票行情、选项卡或新闻项
转动“概览”、“部门”或“加星标” 移至上一个或下一个日期范围
在股票详细信息的任意位置滚动 移动选定的图表样本
箭头键或 h j k l 移动板块、股票行情、排序、图表或新闻选择
Enter 打开选定的板块、股票行情、新闻项目或覆盖选项
Esc 关闭叠加层或上升一级
退格键 打开前一个扇区或股票行情，在任一端换行；删除搜索中的文本
Space 打开下一个扇区或股票行情，在任一端换行；在搜索中插入一个空格
/ 按股票代码或名称搜索缓存的公司
s 打开股票订购
i 在“部门”和“加星标”视图中循环显示单元格值：价格、相对收益、绝对收益、部门相对收益、市值或交易量
o 在概览、部门或加星标视图中反转股票代码顺序
v 在网格和中心向外顺时针螺旋之间切换概览、扇区和加星标热图
F 打开加星号的股票行情
f 对焦点代码加注星标或取消星标
[ / ] 上一个/下一个日期范围
= or + 一步放大到下一个较短的日期范围
- 缩小一步到下一个更长的日期范围
1 至 9 直接选择 1D 到 10Y
0 选择所有可用的历史记录
g，然后 c she t fi mu 开放消费者、服务、医疗保健、能源、技术、金融、工业、材料或公用事业
Alt/Meta + 扇区字母 可选直接形式的同扇区快捷方式
Tab 紧凑的股票视图中的周期图、统计数据和新闻
r 请求立即刷新广泛市场快照
S 打开只读数据状态
? 打开键盘帮助
q 或 Ctrl-C 当没有打开覆盖层时退出并恢复终端

在股票详细信息上，左/右（或 h/l）移动图表光标，而上/下（或 k/j）选择相关新闻行；输入打开它。 退格键和空格键打开原始扇区、加星标列表或基准顺序中的上一个或下一个股票代码，同时保留选定的范围和顺序。

当图表足够宽时，其光标会在轨迹交叉点旁边标记所选价格，并在 X 轴旁边标记所选日期或时间。 详细信息标题总结了缓存的价格观察范围及其开始时间。 除了下一个更短的预设之外，不添加较旧的缓存间隔的范围在详细信息栏中被静音，但仍然完全可单击并保留其键盘快捷键； ALL 始终表示所有缓存的历史记录。

扇区和加星标的单元格显示股票代码加上一个选定的值。 选择排序会重置其方向并选择其自然默认值：按字母顺序排列的估计市值、相对收益、交易量或价格。 然后我独立循环六个可用值。 o 反转概览、扇区和加星标视图中的股票代码顺序。 v 将网格或螺旋放置应用于嵌套的概述扇区热图和展开的扇区/加星标热图。 在可选择股票的视图中，鼠标目标和箭头键导航遵循可见布局；总体投入仍然是部门层面的。 概览重点具有排他性：选择一个基准可以明确行业重点，选择一个行业则可以明确基准重点。

g 扇区前缀仅适用于紧随其后的键。 当它处于武装状态时，Esc 或 Backspace 可以取消它而无需导航；任何其他非扇区键都会取消前缀并保持其正常操作。 鼠标输入和打开覆盖层也会取消待处理的前缀。

在搜索中，键入或粘贴查询，使用向上/向下选择结果，使用 Enter 打开结果，使用 Ctrl-U 清除查询，使用 Esc 关闭。 搜索是本地的，最多返回 20 个缓存的公司匹配项。 当“搜索”打开时，文本键（包括 q、数字和范围快捷键）属于查询。 在帮助和数据状态中，q 关闭叠加层； Esc 关闭每个覆盖层。 激活标题会要求操作系统在默认浏览器中打开其提供商 URL。 如果无法启动浏览器，则通过终端的 OSC 52 剪贴板协议复制 URL。

在缓存准备和提供程序同步期间，辅助页眉或页脚报告已完成/总进度的数字和百分比。 S 打开详细的只读状态视图，而正在运行的应用程序版本在右下角保持可见。

在 ANSI 终端上，stock-tui 明确请求使用 SGR 鼠标编码 (1003 + 1006) 进行全运动跟踪。 因此，它的点击、悬停、拖动和滚轮报告作为文本输入传输，并且不依赖于传统的 X10/onBinary 鼠标传输。 退出时，在恢复原始模式之前报告将被禁用；挂起的事件将被耗尽，未读的输入将被刷新，因此延迟的坐标不会泄漏到下一个 shell 提示符中。

响应式布局

  • 在 60x20 以下，应用程序会显示调整大小提示，而不是绘制重叠内容。
  • 从 60x20 开始，紧凑模式会保留操作导轨并根据可用宽度调整扇区列的数量。 至少，辅助标题行会折叠，因此每个概述扇区都会保留所有五个配对行。
  • 在 120x36 及以上，股票详细信息变成一个分割的工作区，图表和说明位于左侧，统计数据和新闻位于右侧。
  • 概览始终保留 3x3 扇区模型。 短端子将每个 10x10 扇区压缩为成对的半块行，以便所有 100 个颜色信号保持可见。 两个渲染中都保留了网格和螺旋放置。
  • 扇区面板和股票行情图块在给定视口中使用一种固定的单元格大小。 任何不可分割的行或列都会成为平衡的外部填充，而不是拉伸选定的图块。
  • 扇区图块的代码和所选值垂直居中。 当单元格足够大时，星形图块使用细框架，而当单元格不够大时，则保留紧凑的星形标记。

终端在处理鼠标运动、盲文/半块字形、OSC 8 链接、OSC 52 剪贴板访问和 RGB 颜色方面有所不同。 NO_COLOR=1 当颜色不可用时，stock-tui 选择单色调色板。

数据和缓存

实时客户端将版本化的 SEC 衍生候选目录与提供商快照、调整后的柱形图、资产名称/交易所和股票新闻相结合。 它将规范化记录以 WAL 模式存储在每用户 SQLite 数据库中。 默认情况下，后台任务最多每 12 小时检查一次 https://stock.chatcode.dev/catalog/sec-catalog.json 上的紧凑目录。它会在启动时进行检查，并在应用程序保持打开状态时保持该节奏。 第一个屏幕不等待请求。 有效的下载缓存在平台缓存目录下，应用于 SQLite，然后进行提供者宇宙协调；无效、较旧、不可用或过大的响应无法替换最后一个有效的缓存。 当该缓存至少与嵌入式发布目录一样新时，脱机模式将使用该缓存，否则将使用嵌入式目录。

在渲染任何行之前，每个实时缓存都带有活动提供者数据集、端点/提要和市场上下文的标记。 切换到不兼容的提供程序、端点、提要、符号命名空间、货币、时区或常规会话会以事务方式清除不可归因的提供程序行和检查点；带星号的符号保留并由新的提供者重新水化。 市场背景可以涵盖共享同一个日历的多个上市交易所，因此当前的美国热图将纳斯达克、纽约证券交易所和 ARCA 工具放在一起。 发布期间只有一个市场环境处于活跃状态。

新生成的目录包括作为排名代理的 SEC 公众持股量、注明日期、来源标记的股票基础、官方 SIC 行业标签以及由 SEC CIK 锚定的简明 CC0 维基数据公司简介。 当 CIK 仅指向管理法人实体存根或没有有用的配置文件时，构建器会使用规范化的 SEC 发行人名称执行有界实体搜索。 它只接受明确的确切身份或保守的公司名称缩写，并与当前的股票/交易所和业务证据相匹配，然后将项目描述与结构化行业以及在此后备路径上的产品/服务事实相结合。 法律管辖权样板和低信息单一事实输出被拒绝。 宽敞的股票详细信息视图更喜欢生成的公司特定简介，并将交易所、代码和 SIC 标签保留为单独的事实上下文。 当没有安全的维基数据身份可用时，视图将使用可读的 SIC/列表回退，而不是将分类元数据呈现为完整的业务描述。 配置文件查找和散文中使用的每个结构化事实都根据 CIK 存储在持久的 R2 快照中：每日目录出版物获取新的或实质性重命名的发行人，而每月的完整通行证则刷新缓慢变化的描述。 明确的备案涵盖事实自动解决；经过审查的多类别、跟踪股票、Up-C、合伙企业和 SPAC 结构使用精确的类别签名、显式乘数以及来自 data/sec_share_policies.json 的加入范围发行人报告的经济事实。 如果当前行业前 100 名候选人失去其份额基础，则构建器会拒绝陈旧或结构性变化的事实，并导致发布失败。 启动时，客户端刷新候选快照并更喜欢提供商提供的有效市值。 否则，具有公司行动覆盖范围的提供商会在截至日期后调整正向和反向分割的目录份额基础，然后乘以当前价格。 如果所需的拆分查找失败，则本地估计仍然不可用，而不是将过时的份额与拆分后的价格组合起来。 然后，当上限不可用时，通过估计上限或公众持股量来选择每个行业的前 100 名。 公众持股量永远不会显示为市值。 然后，它恢复两年的日线图以及所选 900 家公司和三个基准 ETF 代理的所有提供商可用的每周历史记录。 两个历史计划在最初回填后都使用了 7 天的重叠。 当股票行情打开时，它会懒洋洋地请求范围适当的条形图和 20 个最新头条新闻。 除了特殊的一维快照情况之外，热图交易量更喜欢 2 年的每日柱形图和 5 年、10 年和所有的周柱形图，仅在首选聚合不可用时才使用缓存的替代时间范围。 股票详细信息统计数据继续显示最新会话快照交易量，而实体图表条则使用交易的提供商交易量，而没有仅价格端点的制造数据。 在第一个正成交量柱之后，未占用的柱在昏暗的视觉轨迹中重复前面的高度，直到最后渲染的价格柱；正在进行的会议的未来部分仍然空白。 这不会更改缓存的卷、统计信息、聚合或规模。 1D 在其完整的交易所本地交易窗口中绘制最新观察到的常规交易时段，将未来价格轨迹留空。 1W 连接了最近观察到的 5 个交易日，另一个日内视图省略了休市时段；每日和每周历史使用顺序观察。 开盘交易期间的长差距将最后的交易价格带到下一个观察价格。 会话成员资格是在配置的市场时区中计算的，并且标签以用户的本地时区显示。 在实时模式下，广泛市场快照刷新在启动时立即运行，默认情况下每五分钟运行一次； r 立即启动一个计时器并重新启动该计时器。 单独打开股票代码或更改其范围会触发惰性详细信息请求。 演示和离线模式从不安排远程刷新。 S 只打开状态面板；它不会启动同步。

默认的 Alpaca 适配器仅限于美国股票。 它的提要选择改变了美国场地的覆盖范围；它不支持非美国市场。 Stock-API 合约与提供商无关，但当前的行业目录和 UI 仍然围绕美国上市股票和美元设计。 其他国家、货币、会话和许可来源需要兼容的适配器和明确的产品支持。 公共目录端点仅包含紧凑的 SEC 派生发行人目录；它不是市场价格或新闻代理。

Alpaca 的基本计划目前提供每分钟 200 个历史请求限制以及单一交易所 IEX 的实时美国股票覆盖范围。 默认客户端限制为每分钟 180 个请求。 IEX 价格和交易量与整个市场 SIP 的综合数据不同。 提供商限制和条款可能会发生变化；请参阅 Alpaca 的当前文档。

本地缓存供凭证持有者使用。 Alpaca 声明其 API 数据不能在普通访问条款下重新分发。 不要发布或运送已填充的羊驼缓存。 默认的生产模型是自带密钥，并且没有公共共享密钥价格/新闻服务。 单独运营的 stock-api 端点仅限于明确授权的开发测试，并且不是获得许可的公共市场数据后端。 在提出任何无密钥服务之前，请参阅请求公共显示许可。

扇区模型

该项目有意保留 StockTouch 的九个部门介绍：消费者、服务、医疗保健、能源、技术、金融、工业、材料和公用事业。 这是传统的可视化分类法，而不是当前的 11 扇区 GICS 分类法。 例如，通信服务映射到服务，房地产映射到金融。 地图和目录警告记录在数据提供者中。
